governanceNotes: The reverse direction (poor sleep aggravating dry eye) is documented in the same literature and is recorded as a guard, not as evidence for this edge.
No sleep-disorder-targeted prevalence denominator exists; individual insomnia diagnosis requires excluding primary sleep disorders and psychiatric comorbidity.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Lifelines population cohort (n=71,761) found dry eye associated with poor sleep quality after correction for age, sex, BMI, education, income, and 51 comorbidities including autoimmune and psychiatric disease (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.11-1.28), with 44.9% poor sleep among those with frequent or constant symptoms (Magno 2021); the Miami VA eye-clinic cohort found ocular symptoms tied most strongly to the PSQI sleep-disturbance subscore (OSDI r=0.49, p<0.0005) (Ayoubi 2024).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the Hangzhou community study documents the reverse direction (worse sleep predicting worse dry-eye severity), shared systemic and psychiatric comorbidity partially confounds even the fully adjusted estimate, the veteran-clinic cohort is cross-sectional without severity-exclusion denominators, and insomnia diagnosis at the individual level requires excluding the common primary sleep disorders.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized ocular-pain-arousal pathway: tear-film instability and ocular surface inflammation produce foreign-body sensation and pain that worsen with eye closure and nocturnal tear production; recurring ocular discomfort and arousal repeatedly fragment sleep onset and maintenance, presenting clinically as insomnia. Whether the pattern persists once the ocular surface is controlled is individual and unquantified.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The fully adjusted population estimate is modest (OR 1.20) and residual confounding remains; the strongest symptom-sleep correlations are cross-sectional VA-clinic data; the reverse direction (poor sleep aggravating dry eye via tear osmolarity) is documented; sleep-disorder and psychiatric exclusions are required before any individual attribution.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented dry eye disease with symptom-frequency grading and flare-locked sleep disruption chronology; exclusion of primary insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs, and circadian disorders; psychiatric comorbidity assessment; medication-effect review
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Obstructive sleep apnea and restless legs syndrome
Primary insomnia and circadian rhythm disorders

evidenceGaps: Documented dry eye disease with symptom-frequency grading and flare-locked sleep disruption chronology; exclusion of primary insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs, and circadian disorders; psychiatric comorbidity assessment; medication-effect review
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: the population-grade adjusted association is strong and the mechanism is biologically standard, but bidirectionality is documented in the same literature and cross-sectional designs cannot order the relationship; no causal claim is forced.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The multimodal meta-analysis (26 case-control studies) found dry eye associated with increased depression prevalence (OR 1.83) and, in 48 Mendelian-randomization experiments across two biobanks, supported bidirectional DED-to-DEP and DEP-to-DED causation (Chang 2025, Taipei Veterans General Hospital); the 22-study meta-analysis (n=2,980,026) found depression OR 2.92 (95% CI 2.13-4.01) with severity greatest in primary Sjogren's patients (Wan 2016).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the strongest source itself demonstrates bidirectional causation (depression-to-DED OR 2.34), so one-direction attribution is precluded by the evidence's own design; the Chang MR causation claim is instrument-dependent and has not settled into consensus; Sjogren's strata carry the severity but represent a distinct autoimmune identity; antidepressant treatment itself aggravates dry eye, inverting chronology in treated patients.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized chronic-symptom-burden pathway: persistent ocular pain, visual fluctuation, and functional limitation (reading, screens, driving) impose sustained psychosocial burden; shared immune-activation biology between ocular surface inflammation and depression may amplify the association, presenting clinically as major depressive disorder. Whether any patient's depression is attributable to dry-eye burden versus shared biology or reverse direction is individual and unquantified.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Bidirectional causation is the central finding of the strongest source; the MR instruments are population-specific and contested; Sjogren's strata are a distinct identity; reverse-chronology via antidepressant-induced dry eye must be excluded individually; prevalence does not order the relationship.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented dry eye disease with validated depression-instrument scores (PHQ-9/BDI) and symptom chronology; psychiatric interview establishing independent disorder criteria; autoimmune and Sjogren's assessment; medication-effect review (antidepressants themselves aggravate dry eye)
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Sjogren's syndrome as a shared autoimmune cause of both conditions
